title: Why Angular is a framework where React is a library, and what that buys

videos.script:
This course teaches a framework, and the first thing to know is what that word means. {{calls}} A library is code you call. A framework is code that calls you. You write a class in the shape Angular asks for, and Angular decides when to build it, when to draw it, and when to draw it again.

That one idea explains the rest of today. {{table}} Angular ships its own router, its own forms, its own way to talk to a server, and its own build. A React project chooses each of those. So an Angular team has fewer decisions to make, and a newcomer has more to learn before the first screen.

Then your computer. {{check}} You already have Node and a browser from the JavaScript course. You check them, and you see why this course uses Angular 21 and not 22. {{refuse}} The newest one refuses the Node this track installs, and the message says so in one line.

Then TypeScript, from the beginning. {{types}} Types are checked by the compiler and thrown away before anything runs. You watch Node run a wrong program happily, and the compiler refuse it. {{decorator}} And you write a decorator, which is what every Angular file starts with.

Last, the planner. {{planner}} It is the one application you build across the course, two screens and six study sessions. Work out its first number by hand today. A program prints it in lesson 6.
